summary: King County tree-farm tower built 1942 (1939 per one report), 50 ft with L-6 cab; AWS post 1942-43; removed 1965. Site logged, cables remain.

facts.design: 50-ft pole tower with an L-6 cabin on top; a 1940 ranger cabin is also reported
facts.status_note: Tower and cabin removed (Former Fire Lookout Sites) or destroyed (firelookout.com) in 1965. Late-1990s timber harvest removed or buried remaining foundations; a few logging cables remain on top.

access.note: Later owners Hancock Timber (2003) and Campbell Global (2015) require a non-motorized day-use permit (priced at $8 in 2016 per Willhite Web). Site is on logged timber land; the last half mile is overgrown and must be walked.

visit.trail_note: Willhite Web route from North Bend via Ballarat Street; gate on the left after 7.6 miles of road; 9 miles one way on old railroad grades, the last half mile overgrown and on foot.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Former Fire Lookout Sites, firelookout.com and Willhite Web give 1942 for the tower. Rex's page quotes a 1939 Washington Forest Fire Association report that a 60-foot tower was erected that year, and Willhite Web says a lookout man used a tent in 1939. The story gives both and does not choose.
Three sources give 50 feet for the 1942 tower; the 1939 report quoted on Rex's page gives 60 feet. Height_m uses the 50-foot figure.
Former Fire Lookout Sites says the tower was removed in 1965; Willhite Web says removed or destroyed; firelookout.com says destroyed. The story reports both words.

Former Fire Lookout Sites lists Hancock Insurance Forestry Division as administrator; Willhite Web says the land was Hancock Timber from 2003 and Campbell Global from 2015. The brief's agency is kept, with the ownership history added.

notes_for_editor: Construction date conflict: 1942 (three sources) vs 1939 tower of 60 ft (Rex's page quoting a 1939 WFFA report). Height 50 ft vs 60 ft. Removal: removed (FFLOS, Willhite) vs destroyed (firelookout.com). The permit price is from a 2016 visit report; current permit terms were not found. Access is set to permission for the tree farm. No source describes the site beyond the late-1990s harvest, the cables, and the 2000-2001 photos. The brief's status 'gone' is confirmed.
